onboarding.eyebrow: Your gateway is ready. Connect a client.
onboarding.title: Bring your gateway to your apps and agents
onboarding.description: Choose how you want to use this self-hosted gateway. Start with one action, then explore the services you have connected.
onboarding.prepareHelp: Set the address once. Every example below uses your gateway.
onboarding.gatewayHelp: Use an address reachable from the client. Do not append /v1 or /mcp.
onboarding.urlError: Enter a full HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials, query parameters, or a fragment.
onboarding.tokenHelp: Create a token, then replace <RUNTIME_TOKEN> in the examples. Tokens are never stored on this page.
onboarding.tokenDifference: A Runtime Token authorizes clients to call your gateway. An OOMOL Key enables hosted services inside the gateway. Provider credentials stay on the gateway.
onboarding.localhostHelp: localhost refers to the client’s own device. Use your server address when the gateway runs on another machine.
onboarding.clientTitle: Choose how you will use the gateway
onboarding.clientHelp: All three clients discover and execute the same actions. Pick the workflow that fits your client.
onboarding.mcpTitle: Give your agent access to the gateway
onboarding.mcpHelp: Use an MCP client that supports remote HTTP servers and Authorization headers.
onboarding.mcpConfigure: Copy the configuration into your client’s MCP server settings. Replace the token placeholder if authentication is enabled.
onboarding.mcpDiscover: Ask the agent to use search_actions, then get_action_guide to inspect the selected action.
onboarding.mcpExecute: Try execute_action with the arguments shown on the right. list_connections helps select an account.
onboarding.cliHelp: oo connector sends requests to your own gateway. You do not need to sign in to OOMOL for these commands.
onboarding.cliInstall: Install oo on the machine that will run your commands.
onboarding.cliConfigure: Set the gateway environment variables in the same terminal. They take precedence over saved connections and hosted keys.
onboarding.cliExecute: Search for an action, read its schema, and run it with JSON input.
onboarding.sdkHelp: Use OpenConnector for a self-hosted gateway. It is a thin client; credentials and provider requests stay on the gateway.
onboarding.sdkInstall: Install the SDK in your Node.js or TypeScript project.
onboarding.sdkConfigure: If authentication is enabled, set OOMOL_CONNECT_RUNTIME_TOKEN in your application environment.
onboarding.sdkExecute: Check health, inspect the catalog, and execute the same action from code.
onboarding.tokenEnv: Runtime Token in your application environment
onboarding.nextHelp: Hacker News needs no provider credentials. Next, choose one of your connected services. Every action has CLI and SDK examples.
onboarding.sdkRunHelp: Save the code above as client.mjs, then run it from the same terminal.

errors.title: Operation unsuccessful
errors.encryption: Set OOMOL_CONNECT_ENCRYPTION_KEY and restart Connect before saving the project key. Keep the same encryption key for future starts.
errors.origin: Set OOMOL_CONNECT_ORIGIN to your browser’s Console address and restart. Scheme, host and port must match; localhost and 127.0.0.1 differ.
errors.blocked: The cloud address was blocked. Check proxy Fake-IP and DNS settings so the hostname resolves to a public IP.
errors.dns: Could not resolve the cloud hostname. Check DNS on the machine running Connect.
errors.network: Could not connect to the cloud. Check the Connect machine’s network, proxy and TLS certificates.
errors.redirect: The cloud redirected the request. Redirects are blocked to protect the project key. Check the cloud address.
errors.json: The cloud did not return valid JSON. Check the endpoint, proxy or login interception page.
errors.size: The cloud response exceeded the size limit. Check the cloud service logs.
errors.timeout: The cloud request timed out. Check the network and try again.
errors.key: The project key is invalid or lacks permission. Use an API key from your cloud project, not a Marketplace key.
errors.protocol: The cloud API response is incompatible. Check the deployed cloud and Connect versions.
errors.notFound: The cloud resource was not found. Check the project configuration and API deployment.
errors.inUse: The project is still in use. Switch default authorization methods, remove its connections and resolve pending authorization and cleanup tasks.
errors.mismatch: The project or authorization configuration changed. Refresh and select it again.
errors.rateLimit: Too many requests. Please try again later.
errors.configuration: The cloud project is not configured correctly. Check its key, encryption settings and Console address.
errors.scopes: The cloud OAuth configuration lacks required permissions. Update its scopes in the cloud.
errors.input: Invalid input. Check the project key or selected configuration.
errors.session: Your Console session has expired. Sign in and try again.
errors.unknown: The operation could not be completed. Try again; if it persists, check the Connect server logs.

saas.projectDescription: Connect third-party accounts such as Gmail through OOMOL cloud without configuring an OAuth app locally. Actions on these connections run in the cloud.

saas.keyHint: Enter the API key for your OOMOL cloud project, not a Marketplace key. Saved keys are never displayed. Enter a new key to replace it.
saas.paused: Cleanup is paused. Update the project key to resume.
saas.removeHint: First switch service defaults to local, remove SaaS connections, and resolve pending requests and cleanup tasks. Removing this configuration does not delete the SaaS project.
saas.sourceHint: Applies to new connections only. Existing connections keep their source when reconnecting.
saas.configUnavailableHint: The saved cloud configuration is unavailable. Check the cloud project and its provider configuration, then check again or choose another authorization method.
saas.noConfigs: No compatible cloud configurations are available. Configure a cloud project and a matching provider configuration first.
saas.pending: Waiting for authorization. Keep the completion page open.
saas.manualResult: Authorization could not be confirmed. Check the SaaS project before starting again.
